name: browser_navigate
description: Navigate the active browser tab to the given URL. Waits for the load and returns a fresh accessibility snapshot — no separate browser_snapshot needed. Pass `tab` to drive a specific background tab (index from browser_tabs) without selecting it.

url.description: Absolute URL (must include scheme, e.g. https://...)

tab.description: Tab index from browser_tabs (default: the selected tab)

name: browser_snapshot
description: Capture the current page as a compact accessibility-tree snapshot. Returns url, title, and a YAML-like outline where actionable nodes carry [ref=rN] handles. Use these refs in browser_click and browser_type. This is the primary way to "see" the page — far cheaper than dumping HTML or screenshots. By default only what is painted inside the viewport is returned; hidden, overlay-covered and off-screen nodes are omitted and summarised as scroll hints. Scroll (browser_scroll) to reach them, or pass full=true when you genuinely need the whole document. Pass `tab` to snapshot a specific tab (index from browser_tabs) — refs are per-tab, so acting on them (browser_click/browser_type) needs the same `tab`.

full.description: Return the entire document instead of the viewport-filtered tree (much larger; default false)

tab.description: Tab index from browser_tabs (default: the selected tab)

name: browser_click
description: Click the element identified by ref (from the latest browser_snapshot). Scrolls into view, performs a human-like mouse move, then clicks. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards. Refs from the previous snapshot are now stale. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) when the ref came from a background tab's snapshot — refs are per-tab.

tab.description: Tab the ref belongs to (browser_tabs index; default: the selected tab)

name: browser_hover
description: Hover over the element identified by ref (from the latest browser_snapshot). Scrolls into view and performs a human-like mouse move WITHOUT clicking — use it to open hover-triggered dropdown menus, tooltips and mega-navs. Returns a fresh snapshot so the hover-revealed content is visible. Refs from the previous snapshot are now stale. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) when the ref came from a background tab's snapshot — refs are per-tab.

tab.description: Tab the ref belongs to (browser_tabs index; default: the selected tab)

name: browser_type
description: Move the cursor to the input/textarea identified by ref, click to focus, then type the text with realistic per-keystroke timing. Press Enter with submit=true (default false). Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards. Refs from the previous snapshot are now stale. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) when the ref came from a background tab's snapshot — refs are per-tab.

text.description: Text to put into the field

submit.description: If true, dispatches an Enter keydown after typing (default false)

tab.description: Tab the ref belongs to (browser_tabs index; default: the selected tab)

name: browser_scroll_element
description: Scroll a container identified by ref, rather than the window. browser_scroll moves the page, which does nothing for a list, drawer or chat log that scrolls inside its own box — those show as [scrollable +Npx] in the snapshot. Stepped, so lazy-loading handlers fire. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

ref.description: Ref of the scroll container, e.g. "r15"

deltaY.description: Pixels to scroll; negative scrolls up

name: browser_draw
description: Press, move and release inside ONE element — a canvas stroke, a signature pad, a colour picker, a range track. browser_drag goes between two elements and cannot express a gesture that starts and ends on the same surface. Points are fractions of the element box (0..1), so 0.1,0.5 to 0.9,0.5 draws a horizontal line across the middle. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

ref.description: Ref of the surface to draw on, e.g. "r24"

from.description: Start point as fractions of the element box, e.g. {"x":0.1,"y":0.5}

to.description: End point as fractions of the element box

name: browser_paste
description: Put text on the clipboard and paste it into the element identified by ref. A page that reads clipboardData on a paste event sees nothing when the text is typed instead — the two are different events. Overwrites the real clipboard. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

ref.description: Ref of the field to paste into, e.g. "r22"

text.description: Text to place on the clipboard and paste

name: browser_tabs
description: List the open browser tabs, switch to one, or open a new background tab. A window.open popup becomes a tab, and its content is unreachable until the tools are pointed at it — every other browser tool acts on the selected tab only. Select by index from the list. open loads a URL in a new tab WITHOUT switching to it, so several same-site pages can load in parallel; read each with list_endpoints({tab}) / list_requests({tab}).

index.description: Tab index to select, from the list output

name: browser_handle_dialog
description: Choose the answer for a page alert()/confirm()/prompt(). Dialogs that open while your tools run are answered automatically (OK / the prompt default) and listed at the end of that tool's result. Call this BEFORE the click to reach a "Cancel" branch or type a prompt value. One-shot: consumed by the first dialog.

accept.description: true for OK, false for Cancel (a cancelled prompt returns null)

promptText.description: Value a prompt() should return. Ignored when accept is false.

name: browser_file_upload
description: Attach files to a file input identified by ref. A file input cannot be typed into — the browser owns its value — and clicking it opens a native picker no tool can answer, so this is the only way to fill one. The ref may point at the input or at its rendered button. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

ref.description: Ref of the file input, or of its button, e.g. "r7"

paths.description: Absolute paths of the files to attach. Pass several only for a multiple input.

name: browser_history
description: Move back or forward in the tab's own history. browser_navigate to the previous URL is NOT the same thing: it pushes a new entry, so the page sees a fresh load rather than a restore and anything keyed off popstate or history length behaves differently. Errors when there is nothing to go to. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

name: browser_click_modified
description: Click a ref with a non-default button or click count: right-click to open a context menu, or double-click. browser_click always sends a single left click, and two browser_click calls are seconds apart so the page never pairs them into a double-click. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

name: browser_drag
description: Drag one ref onto another. Tries the browser's own drag machinery first (HTML5 draggable), then falls back to a held-button pointer gesture, which is what dnd-kit / SortableJS listen for. A click on the source followed by a click on the target is two unrelated clicks and neither sees a drag. The result says which mechanism ran — CHECK THE PAGE ACTUALLY CHANGED, a drag that reached nothing looks identical to one that worked. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

from.description: Ref of the element to drag, e.g. "r6"

to.description: Ref of the drop target, e.g. "r9"

name: browser_press_key
description: Send a single key to the focused element — the only way to reach a keyboard-driven widget. Escape closes a dialog, ArrowDown moves a listbox or a slider, Tab moves focus, and Control+A then Delete clears a field (browser_type appends rather than replacing). Pass ref to focus that element first WITHOUT clicking it, which matters when a click would dismiss or mis-select. Accepts one character, or: Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, Delete, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Space. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

key.description: Key name (e.g. "Escape", "ArrowDown") or a single character

ref.description: Focus this element first, without clicking it. Omit to send to whatever has focus.

modifiers.description: Held while the key is pressed, e.g. ["Control"] for Control+A

name: browser_select_option
description: Choose option(s) in a <select> identified by ref (from the latest browser_snapshot). A native dropdown is drawn by the OS, so browser_click and browser_type cannot reach its options — this is the only way to answer one. Match by option value or by visible label; if nothing matches, the error lists the available options. Returns a fresh snapshot — DO NOT call browser_snapshot afterwards.

ref.description: Element ref of the <select> from browser_snapshot, e.g. "r20"

values.description: Option values or visible labels to select. Pass one for a normal select, several for a multiple one.

name: browser_click_selector
description: Click the first element matching a CSS selector, using the SAME human-shaped cursor move + click as browser_click (visualised on the page, fires trusted events). Use this to interact when you located an element via dom_extract / browser_evaluate and have no snapshot ref — NEVER poke the DOM with raw JS (.click()/dispatchEvent) to interact, as that skips the cursor animation and trips bot detection. Returns a fresh snapshot.

selector.description: CSS selector for the target, e.g. "#q" or "button.search-btn"

name: browser_hover_selector
description: Hover over the first element matching a CSS selector, using the SAME human-shaped cursor move as browser_hover (no click). Use when you have a selector but no snapshot ref — NEVER fake hover with raw JS dispatchEvent, as that skips the cursor animation and fires untrusted events. Returns a fresh snapshot.

selector.description: CSS selector for the target, e.g. "nav .menu-item"

name: browser_type_selector
description: Type into the first element matching a CSS selector, using the SAME human-shaped focus + per-keystroke timing as browser_type (visualised, fires real trusted key events that survive bot detection). Use when you have a selector but no snapshot ref. Set submit=true to press Enter after typing. Returns a fresh snapshot — do NOT set the value with raw JS.

selector.description: CSS selector for the input/textarea, e.g. "#q"

text.description: Text to type into the field

submit.description: If true, presses Enter after typing (default false)

name: browser_scroll
description: Scroll the page. Provide either absolute y or relative deltaY (in pixels). Useful for infinite-scroll sites.

y.description: Absolute scroll position in px from top

deltaY.description: Relative scroll delta in px (positive = down)

name: set_viewport
description: Switch the active browser tab between desktop and mobile mode (changes user-agent + device metrics) and reloads the page. Use mobile mode to access mobile-only sites or APIs.

name: browser_evaluate
description: Run a JavaScript expression in the active page and return the result. The expression must return a JSON-serialisable value. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) to run it in a background tab without selecting it.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate (must return a value)

tab.description: Tab index from browser_tabs (default: the selected tab)

name: dom_extract
description: Extract structured data from the rendered DOM by CSS selector. For each matching element, pulls the requested fields (text/href/src/value/html) plus any named attributes. This is the primary way to scrape results from server-rendered (SSR) pages — no JSON API required. Prefer this over ad-hoc browser_evaluate for pulling lists (search results, tables, cards).

fields.description: Built-in fields to pull per node. Default ['text'].

attrs.description: Extra attribute names to read, e.g. ["data-id","aria-label"]

limit.description: Max nodes to return (default 50). Guards against huge dumps.

name: browser_screenshot
description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current page (visible area). Returned as image content. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) to shoot a background tab without selecting it.

tab.description: Tab index from browser_tabs (default: the selected tab)

name: ui_crawl
description: Red Team exhaustive-click crawler: deterministically clicks every actionable element on the page once, attributes the requests each fired (button→API map), and returns the discovered endpoints for the probe phase. On non-loopback hosts, mutating requests are captured and answered with a synthetic 204 by the capture-not-send fence — the server state is never changed; loopback / lab_target hosts pass through so local benchmarks can be confirmed. Pass `tab` (browser_tabs index) to crawl a background tab.

tab.description: Tab index from browser_tabs (default: the selected tab)

maxElements.description: Max elements to click (default 40, hard cap 150)

name: browser_wait_for
description: Wait until the page settles before you read it — poll until a CSS selector is present (and visible) and/or a piece of text appears in the DOM. Use this on SPA / JS-rendered pages where the first snapshot shows a spinner or empty list because content arrives via a later XHR, instead of snapshotting repeatedly. Give at least one of selector / text; when both are given, both must hold.

selector.description: CSS selector to wait for (must exist and be visible)

text.description: Substring to wait for anywhere in the page text

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this many ms (default 8000)
